confidence_note: Based on established HPLC maintenance best practices from major manufacturers (Agilent, Waters, Shimadzu).

materials_needed.name: HPLC-grade isopropanol
materials_needed.purpose: Flushing solvent lines and pump heads

before_cleaning: Allow system to finish any running sequence and return to idle state.
Reduce flow rate to 0 mL/min and turn off column oven.
Remove the analytical column and replace with a union or restriction capillary.
Note the current method parameters for restoration after cleaning.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with water
cleaning_steps.description: Pump 100% HPLC-grade water through the system at 0.5 mL/min for 15 minutes to remove buffer salts.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with methanol
cleaning_steps.description: Switch to 100% methanol and flush at 0.5 mL/min for 15 minutes.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with isopropanol
cleaning_steps.description: Switch to 100% isopropanol and flush at 0.3 mL/min for 10 minutes to remove hydrophobic contaminants.
warnings: Reduce flow rate for IPA due to higher viscosity.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean autosampler needle
cleaning_steps.description: Run the needle wash cycle 3–5 times with 50:50 MeOH:H₂O. Inspect needle for bends or burrs.

cleaning_steps.title: Inspect and replace inlet frits
cleaning_steps.description: Check solvent inlet frits for discoloration or blockage. Replace if flow is restricted.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean detector flow cell
cleaning_steps.description: Flush the UV/DAD flow cell with methanol for 10 minutes. For stubborn contamination, use 1N NaOH (avoid with certain cell types).
warnings: Do not use NaOH on stainless steel flow cells without checking manufacturer compatibility.

cleaning_steps.title: Purge and degas
cleaning_steps.description: Purge all solvent lines and run the degasser for at least 5 minutes with the final mobile phase.

cleaning_steps.title: Restore system
cleaning_steps.description: Reconnect the column, set flow to operating conditions, and equilibrate for 20–30 minutes before running samples.

after_cleaning: Run a blank injection to verify baseline stability.
Check for leaks at all fittings.
Verify retention time and peak shape with a system suitability standard.
Log cleaning date and activities in the instrument logbook.
what_not_to_do: Never run buffers through the system without flushing with water first — salt precipitation will block capillaries.
Do not use acetone in PEEK-based systems — it can swell and damage PEEK tubing and fittings.
Never exceed the column's maximum pressure rating during flushing.
Do not leave the system filled with pure water for extended periods — microbial growth will occur.
Never use abrasive materials to clean the autosampler needle.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Flush with organic solvent at end of each day. Full system cleaning weekly or after 500 injections.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Immediately flush with appropriate solvent series (water → methanol → IPA → methanol → mobile phase).
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace inlet frits monthly. Replace pump seals every 6–12 months or per manufacturer schedule.

safety_warnings: Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses when handling organic solvents.
Ensure adequate ventilation — methanol and IPA vapors are flammable.
Dispose of waste solvents in designated waste containers according to local regulations.
Allow the column oven to cool before handling.
notes: If using phosphate buffers, always flush with water before switching to organic solvents.
For reversed-phase systems, the flush sequence is: water → methanol → IPA → methanol → mobile phase.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on UHPLC maintenance practices from Agilent 1290, Waters ACQUITY, and Thermo Vanquish documentation.
before_cleaning: Complete any running sequence and return system to standby.
Reduce flow to 0 mL/min and turn off column thermostat.
Remove the UHPLC column — replace with a zero-dead-volume union.
Record current method parameters.

cleaning_steps.title: Low-pressure water flush
cleaning_steps.description: Flush with UHPLC-grade water at 0.3 mL/min for 15 minutes to remove all buffer salts.
warnings: Use low flow rate to avoid pressure spikes without column.

cleaning_steps.title: Methanol flush
cleaning_steps.description: Switch to 100% methanol at 0.3 mL/min for 15 minutes.

cleaning_steps.title: IPA flush
cleaning_steps.description: Flush with isopropanol at 0.2 mL/min for 10 minutes for deep cleaning.
warnings: Use reduced flow — IPA viscosity generates high backpressure in UHPLC systems.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean injection system
cleaning_steps.description: Run automated needle wash cycles. Inspect needle seat and rotor seal for wear.

cleaning_steps.title: Inspect inline filters
cleaning_steps.description: Check and replace 0.2 µm inline filters if pressure has increased above baseline.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush detector cell
cleaning_steps.description: Flush UV/DAD cell with methanol for 10 minutes at low flow.

cleaning_steps.title: Return to mobile phase
cleaning_steps.description: Flush back through methanol to water (if aqueous method) or directly to mobile phase composition.

cleaning_steps.title: Reconnect column and equilibrate
cleaning_steps.description: Install column, ramp flow to operating rate, equilibrate for 30 minutes.

after_cleaning: Run a blank gradient to verify baseline and pressure stability.
Check all fittings for leaks — UHPLC pressures amplify small leaks.
Run system suitability test with a reference standard.
Record cleaning in instrument logbook.
what_not_to_do: Never use unfiltered solvents — particulates will instantly block sub-2 µm column frits.
Do not exceed 0.3 mL/min when flushing without a column — overpressure may damage the detector cell.
Never switch directly from high-salt buffers to high-organic without an intermediate water flush.
Do not use acetone in systems with PEEK components.
Never overtighten UHPLC fittings — finger-tight plus 1/4 turn maximum.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Daily flush at end of run sequence. Full cleaning weekly.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Immediate flush sequence: water → MeOH → IPA → MeOH → mobile phase.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace needle seal and rotor seal every 3–6 months. Replace inlet frits monthly.

safety_warnings: UHPLC systems operate at very high pressures (up to 1300 bar). Never open fittings while pressurized.
Wear gloves and safety glasses when handling solvents.
Ensure waste lines are properly routed to waste containers.
notes: UHPLC systems are more sensitive to particulates than standard HPLC — always use pre-filtered solvents.
Keep a log of system pressure readings to detect gradual blockage trends.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on LCMS maintenance practices from Agilent 6100/6400 series, Waters Xevo/QDa, and Thermo ISQ/TSQ documentation.
before_cleaning: Allow the MS source to cool completely (wait at least 30 minutes after turning off).
Vent the MS vacuum system following the manufacturer's vent procedure.
Set the LC to standby with 0 mL/min flow.
Wear nitrile gloves — skin oils contaminate MS source components.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush LC system
cleaning_steps.description: Flush the LC with water for 15 min, then methanol for 15 min (same as HPLC cleaning).

cleaning_steps.title: Remove ESI source components
cleaning_steps.description: Remove spray shield (cone), sampling cone / capillary cap, and ion transfer capillary according to manufacturer instructions.
warnings: Handle components with gloved hands only. Note orientation for reassembly.

cleaning_steps.title: Sonicate source parts
cleaning_steps.description: Place removable metal parts in 50:50 MeOH:H₂O and sonicate for 10–15 minutes.
warnings: Do not sonicate plastic or PEEK parts.

cleaning_steps.title: Wipe source housing
cleaning_steps.description: Wipe the interior of the source housing with lint-free wipes dampened with IPA. Remove visible deposits.
warnings: Do not spray solvent directly into the MS vacuum inlet.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean ion transfer capillary
cleaning_steps.description: If removable, soak in IPA or sonicate. If fixed, flush with IPA using a syringe. Let dry completely.
warnings: Ensure capillary is completely dry before reinstalling.

cleaning_steps.title: Reassemble source
cleaning_steps.description: Reinstall all components in reverse order. Ensure proper alignment and seating.

cleaning_steps.title: Pump down and stabilize
cleaning_steps.description: Close the source door, allow the vacuum to pump down to operating pressure. Wait for stable vacuum readings.

cleaning_steps.title: Verify performance
cleaning_steps.description: Run an autotune or system check with calibrant solution. Verify signal intensity meets specifications.

after_cleaning: Compare autotune results to previous values — sensitivity should be restored.
Run a system suitability injection to verify chromatographic and MS performance.
Check for leaks at all LC and MS connections.
Log cleaning date, components cleaned, and tune results.
what_not_to_do: Never use non-LC-MS grade solvents — additives cause ion suppression and contaminate the source.
Never touch source components with bare hands — fingerprint oils cause persistent background ions.
Do not use abrasive materials on any MS source surface.
Never spray solvent directly into the vacuum inlet or mass analyzer.
Do not operate the MS with a dirty source — it will contaminate deeper (harder to clean) components.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Clean ESI source every 1–2 weeks or when sensitivity drops >30%.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Immediately clean source and flush LC if non-volatile buffers or detergents were accidentally introduced.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Monthly source inspection. Replace ESI needle/capillary per manufacturer schedule (typically every 6 months).

safety_warnings: Allow source to cool completely before handling — temperatures can exceed 300°C.
The MS vacuum system contains high voltage — never open covers beyond the source area.
Use proper PPE: nitrile gloves, safety glasses, lab coat.
Some MS systems use radioactive ion sources — check your specific instrument.
notes: Keep a 'tune history' log to track sensitivity trends — gradual decline indicates source contamination.
For APCI or APPI sources, cleaning procedures differ — consult the specific source manual.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on GC maintenance practices from Agilent 7890/8890, Shimadzu GC-2030, and Thermo TRACE series documentation.
before_cleaning: Cool the inlet and oven to room temperature.
Turn off carrier gas flow and detector gases (H₂, air).
Allow FID or other detector to cool completely.
Remove the analytical column from the inlet (note insertion depth).

cleaning_steps.title: Replace inlet septum
cleaning_steps.description: Remove the old septum and install a new low-bleed septum. Ensure proper seating.

cleaning_steps.title: Remove and clean/replace inlet liner
cleaning_steps.description: Remove the liner. For reusable liners, sonicate in methanol for 15 min, then bake at 250°C. Or install a new deactivated liner.
warnings: Always use deactivated liners — active surfaces cause peak tailing for polar compounds.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean inlet body
cleaning_steps.description: With liner removed, use a lint-free swab dampened with methanol to clean the inlet body interior.
warnings: Never use metal tools that could scratch the inlet bore.

cleaning_steps.title: Trim column end
cleaning_steps.description: Using a ceramic cutter, trim 5–10 cm from the column inlet end to remove any contaminated or damaged stationary phase.
warnings: Always score and snap — never use scissors or metal blades on fused silica.

cleaning_steps.title: Reinstall column
cleaning_steps.description: Insert column into inlet at the correct depth (per manufacturer specs), tighten ferrule, restore carrier gas flow, and leak-check.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean FID jet and collector
cleaning_steps.description: If FID sensitivity has decreased, remove and sonicate the jet in methanol. Clean collector with a soft brush.
warnings: The FID jet is fragile — handle carefully.

cleaning_steps.title: Bake out column
cleaning_steps.description: Heat the column 20°C above normal operating temperature (but below max column temp) for 30–60 min with carrier gas flowing.
warnings: Do not exceed the column's maximum temperature rating.

cleaning_steps.title: Verify performance
cleaning_steps.description: Run a blank injection to check baseline. Then run a test mix to verify peak shape and retention times.

after_cleaning: Leak-check all connections with an electronic leak detector or soap solution.
Verify baseline stability and absence of ghost peaks with blank runs.
Run a system suitability standard.
Record maintenance in the instrument logbook.
what_not_to_do: Never use ungloved hands to handle liners, columns, or ferrules — skin oils cause ghost peaks.
Do not use metal tools inside the inlet bore — scratches create active sites.
Never exceed the column's maximum temperature during bakeout.
Do not forget to turn off hydrogen gas before opening the FID.
Never cut fused silica columns with metal blades — use ceramic cutters only.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Replace septum every 50–100 injections. Replace liner every 100–200 injections or when active-compound tailing appears.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Trim column end, replace liner and septum, bake out column.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace O-ring and gold seal annually. Clean FID jet every 6 months.

safety_warnings: GC inlets operate at high temperatures (up to 400°C) — allow complete cooling before maintenance.
Hydrogen carrier gas is explosive — turn off H₂ and verify no leaks before any maintenance.
Fused silica column fragments are sharp — handle with care and dispose properly.
Ensure adequate ventilation when using hexane or dichloromethane.
notes: Keep a septum and liner replacement log to track injection count vs. maintenance intervals.
If ghost peaks persist after cleaning, the column may need replacement.

Vent the MS vacuum system using the manufacturer's vent procedure.
Allow the ion source to cool completely.

cleaning_steps.title: GC inlet maintenance
cleaning_steps.description: Replace septum, clean/replace liner, trim column end. Follow the standard GC cleaning procedure.

cleaning_steps.title: Vent MS and remove source
cleaning_steps.description: Follow the vent procedure, then carefully remove the EI/CI ion source assembly.
warnings: Note the orientation and order of components for reassembly.

cleaning_steps.title: Disassemble ion source
cleaning_steps.description: Separate repeller, ion volume, lenses, and other removable parts per manufacturer instructions.

cleaning_steps.title: Sonicate source parts
cleaning_steps.description: Sonicate all metal parts in methanol for 15 min, then in hexane for 10 min. For heavily contaminated sources, gently polish with alumina slurry.
warnings: Do not polish filaments or electron multiplier. Only polish designated metal surfaces.

cleaning_steps.title: Dry components
cleaning_steps.description: Air dry on lint-free wipes, then bake in a clean oven at 100°C for 30 min (if available).

cleaning_steps.title: Reassemble and install source
cleaning_steps.description: Reassemble in correct order and orientation. Install source and ensure proper seating.

cleaning_steps.title: Pump down
cleaning_steps.description: Close the vent valve and allow the system to reach operating vacuum (typically <5 × 10⁻⁵ Torr).

cleaning_steps.title: Autotune and verify
cleaning_steps.description: Run an autotune with PFTBA or other tuning compound. Compare to previous tune reports.

after_cleaning: Verify tune values are within specification (compare to factory tune).
Run a blank to check for background contamination.
Run a sensitivity check standard at the method detection limit.
Record all maintenance, tune values, and cleaning details.
what_not_to_do: Never touch ion source parts with bare hands — fingerprints cause persistent m/z background peaks.
Do not polish the filament or electron multiplier — these are delicate and easily damaged.
Never use non-GC-MS grade solvents for source cleaning.
Do not rush the pump-down — operating at poor vacuum damages the filament and detector.
Never open the MS vacuum chamber without following the proper vent procedure.

cleaning_frequency.routine: GC inlet: septum/liner per GC schedule. MS source: every 3–6 months or when tune values degrade.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Immediately vent and clean source if non-volatile matrix was injected without proper sample prep.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace filament annually. Replace electron multiplier when gain exceeds manufacturer threshold.

safety_warnings: The MS ion source operates at high voltage — always vent and power down before maintenance.
Allow complete cooling before handling source components.
Hydrogen carrier gas is explosive — follow GC hydrogen safety protocols.
Dispose of cleaning solvents in designated waste.
notes: Track autotune EM voltage over time — steadily increasing voltage indicates detector aging.
A properly cleaned source should restore sensitivity to within 80% of factory specifications.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on IC maintenance from Thermo Dionex ICS series and Metrohm IC documentation.
before_cleaning: Set flow to 0 mL/min and stop the pump.
Remove the analytical column and suppressor.
Prepare fresh eluent — old eluent absorbs CO₂ and degrades.
Note current operating parameters.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush system with DI water
cleaning_steps.description: Flush all eluent lines with fresh 18.2 MΩ DI water for 15 minutes at operating flow rate.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean eluent reservoir
cleaning_steps.description: Rinse eluent bottles with DI water 3 times. Prepare fresh eluent using IC-grade reagents.
warnings: NaOH eluents absorb atmospheric CO₂ rapidly — minimize exposure time.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean or replace pump tubing
cleaning_steps.description: Inspect peristaltic pump tubing for wear. Replace if flattened or cracked.

cleaning_steps.title: Regenerate suppressor
cleaning_steps.description: Follow the manufacturer's suppressor regeneration procedure. For electrolytic suppressors, run the recommended regeneration cycle.
warnings: Do not use organic solvents with suppressors.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean conductivity cell
cleaning_steps.description: Flush the conductivity cell with DI water for 10 minutes. Check cell constant is within spec.

cleaning_steps.title: Reassemble and equilibrate
cleaning_steps.description: Reconnect column and suppressor, start flow with fresh eluent, equilibrate until baseline is stable.

after_cleaning: Check baseline conductivity — should be low and stable.
Run a multi-ion standard to verify peak identification and quantitation.
Inspect for leaks at all connections.
Record maintenance in logbook.
what_not_to_do: Never use organic solvents in the IC system — they damage suppressors and columns.
Do not use metal fittings — metal ions contaminate the system and appear as cation peaks.
Never let eluent bottles run dry — air entering the system causes baseline instability.
Do not use tap water or low-grade water — trace ions will contaminate the entire system.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Prepare fresh eluent weekly. Flush system with DI water at end of each day.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Flush extensively with DI water. Replace guard column if contaminated.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace pump tubing monthly. Regenerate or replace suppressor per manufacturer schedule.

safety_warnings: NaOH solutions are corrosive — wear gloves and eye protection.
MSA is corrosive — handle with care.
Ensure waste is properly neutralized before disposal.
notes: IC systems are extremely sensitive to contamination — always use the highest purity water and reagents.
Store NaOH eluent under nitrogen or helium to prevent carbonate formation.

before_cleaning: Remove vials from the carousel.
Note the current capillary length and window position.
Set the instrument to manual rinse mode.
Prepare fresh conditioning solutions.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with 1 M NaOH
cleaning_steps.description: Rinse capillary with 1 M NaOH for 10 minutes at high pressure to regenerate silanol groups.
warnings: NaOH is corrosive — handle with care.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with DI water
cleaning_steps.description: Rinse with DI water for 5 minutes to remove NaOH.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with 0.1 M HCl
cleaning_steps.description: Rinse with HCl for 5 minutes to neutralize and protonate surface.

cleaning_steps.title: Final DI water rinse
cleaning_steps.description: Rinse with DI water for 10 minutes.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with running buffer
cleaning_steps.description: Condition capillary with fresh running buffer for 10 minutes.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean electrode assemblies
cleaning_steps.description: Wipe inlet and outlet electrodes with lint-free wipes dampened with DI water.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean vial positions
cleaning_steps.description: Clean the carousel/tray and check for buffer crystallization or spills.

after_cleaning: Run a test separation to verify EOF and migration time reproducibility.
Check current stability during a run — erratic current indicates capillary problems.
Record capillary conditioning details and number of runs.
what_not_to_do: Never use a capillary with a blocked or cracked detection window.
Do not skip the conditioning steps — inconsistent EOF causes irreproducible separations.
Never allow the capillary to dry out during storage — store filled with DI water.
Do not apply voltage with an empty capillary — this damages the capillary coating.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Condition capillary with NaOH/water/buffer sequence at start of each day.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Extended NaOH flush (30 min) followed by full conditioning sequence.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace capillary every 100–200 runs or when migration time reproducibility degrades.

safety_warnings: NaOH and HCl are corrosive — wear gloves and eye protection.
High voltage (up to 30 kV) is used during CE operation — never open the instrument during a run.
Fused silica capillary fragments are extremely sharp.
notes: For coated capillaries, follow the specific coating manufacturer's conditioning protocol instead.
Track EOF marker migration times to monitor capillary health over time.

confidence_note: Based on SFC maintenance from Waters ACQUITY UPC² and Agilent 1260 SFC documentation.
before_cleaning: Stop CO₂ flow and allow system pressure to drop to ambient.
Set co-solvent pump to 0 mL/min.
Remove the SFC column.
Allow back-pressure regulator (BPR) to depressurize fully.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush co-solvent lines
cleaning_steps.description: Flush all co-solvent channels with methanol at 1 mL/min for 15 minutes.

cleaning_steps.title: IPA flush
cleaning_steps.description: Flush with isopropanol at 0.5 mL/min for 10 minutes to remove non-polar residues.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean BPR
cleaning_steps.description: Flush the back-pressure regulator with methanol. If BPR pressure is erratic, follow manufacturer's BPR cleaning or replacement procedure.
warnings: BPR is a precision component — do not disassemble without manufacturer instructions.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean detector cell
cleaning_steps.description: Flush UV or PDA cell with methanol for 10 minutes.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean gas-liquid separator
cleaning_steps.description: If equipped, flush the waste/make-up flow path. Check for blockages.

cleaning_steps.title: Purge CO₂ lines
cleaning_steps.description: Briefly pressurize and depressurize the CO₂ path to clear any condensed moisture.

cleaning_steps.title: Reconnect and equilibrate
cleaning_steps.description: Install column, start CO₂ flow, set BPR pressure, and equilibrate for 20 minutes.

after_cleaning: Verify stable BPR pressure and flow rate.
Run a blank injection to check baseline.
Run a test standard to verify retention and peak shape.
Record maintenance in logbook.
what_not_to_do: Never open fittings while the system is pressurized — CO₂ expansion is rapid and can cause frostbite.
Do not use water in the CO₂ path — ice formation will block the system.
Never use non-SFC-grade CO₂ — impurities affect chromatography and damage components.
Do not leave co-solvent channels filled with buffer solutions.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Flush co-solvent lines at end of each day. Full cleaning monthly.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Flush with MeOH → IPA → MeOH sequence. Clean BPR if pressure is erratic.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace BPR seal annually. Check CO₂ cylinder purity with each replacement.

safety_warnings: SFC systems operate at high pressure (up to 400+ bar) — never loosen fittings while pressurized.
CO₂ release causes rapid cooling — risk of frostbite. Ensure adequate ventilation.
CO₂ is an asphyxiant in enclosed spaces — ensure room has CO₂ monitoring.
Wear safety glasses and gloves during maintenance.
notes: SFC systems are sensitive to moisture — always use dry, high-purity CO₂.
If the BPR becomes difficult to control, it likely needs seal replacement.

confidence_note: Based on TGA maintenance from TA Instruments Discovery/Q-series and NETZSCH TG 209 documentation.
before_cleaning: Allow the furnace to cool to room temperature (wait at least 1 hour after a high-temperature run).
Close the purge gas flow.
Remove the sample pan from the balance arm.
Open the furnace per manufacturer instructions.

cleaning_steps.title: Remove sample residue
cleaning_steps.description: Carefully remove any spilled sample material from the furnace tube using a soft brush. Work gently to avoid disturbing the thermocouple.
warnings: Do not touch the thermocouple or balance mechanism with tools.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean or replace crucibles
cleaning_steps.description: For platinum pans: heat to 1000°C in air to burn off residue, then cool. For alumina pans: dispose and use new ones.
warnings: Handle platinum pans with clean forceps only.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean furnace tube
cleaning_steps.description: Wipe accessible interior surfaces with a lint-free wipe. For stubborn deposits, carefully use a cotton swab with IPA.
warnings: Do not use excessive liquid — it can damage the thermocouple and heating elements.

cleaning_steps.title: Inspect thermocouple
cleaning_steps.description: Visually check the thermocouple for corrosion, discoloration, or deposits. Clean gently if needed.
warnings: Thermocouple wires are extremely fragile — do not bend or apply pressure.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean balance chamber
cleaning_steps.description: Use a soft brush and gentle air flow to remove any dust or particles from the microbalance area.
warnings: Never blow compressed air directly at the balance mechanism — use gentle flow only.

cleaning_steps.title: Purge and verify
cleaning_steps.description: Close the furnace, run a purge with dry N₂ for 10 minutes, then run a blank (empty pan) to verify baseline.

after_cleaning: Run a blank measurement to verify flat baseline (weight change <0.02 mg over full temperature range).
Run a calcium oxalate or indium calibration standard to verify temperature accuracy.
Record cleaning date and any component replacements.
Check gas flow rates with a flow meter.
what_not_to_do: Never touch the microbalance mechanism or hangdown wire — it is extremely sensitive.
Do not use water or aqueous solutions to clean inside the furnace.
Never run corrosive samples (strong acids, HF) without appropriate protective liners.
Do not exceed the maximum temperature rating of your crucible type.
Never force the furnace open or closed — this can damage alignment.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Clean crucibles after each run. Clean furnace interior weekly.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Immediately clean any sample spillage. Run burnout at 900°C in air if organic contamination is suspected.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Calibrate temperature and weight quarterly. Replace thermocouple per manufacturer schedule.

safety_warnings: The furnace reaches temperatures up to 1000°C+ — allow complete cooling before maintenance.
Some samples release toxic gases during heating — always use adequate exhaust ventilation.
Wear heat-resistant gloves when handling recently heated components.
notes: Always use the correct gas atmosphere (N₂, air, Ar) for your application — using the wrong gas invalidates results.
Buoyancy correction blanks should be run after any furnace cleaning or gas change.

confidence_note: Based on DSC maintenance from TA Instruments Discovery/Q-series and NETZSCH DSC documentation.
before_cleaning: Allow the DSC cell to cool to room temperature.
Remove any sample pans from the cell.
Turn off purge gas temporarily for cleaning access.

cleaning_steps.title: Remove sample debris
cleaning_steps.description: Carefully remove any pan residue or spilled sample from the DSC cell using soft forceps and a brush.
warnings: Do not scratch the sensor surface — it is precision-machined.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean cell with IPA
cleaning_steps.description: Dampen a lint-free wipe or cotton swab with IPA and gently clean the sample and reference platforms.
warnings: Do not flood the cell with liquid.

cleaning_steps.title: Burn off organic residue
cleaning_steps.description: Run the DSC to 600°C (or cell maximum) in air or oxygen atmosphere for 10 minutes to oxidize organic contaminants.
warnings: Only do this if your DSC cell type supports high-temperature burnout. Check manual.

cleaning_steps.title: Cool and inspect
cleaning_steps.description: Cool to room temperature. Inspect the sensor surface for discoloration or deposits.

cleaning_steps.title: Verify with baseline
cleaning_steps.description: Run a baseline scan (empty cell, both positions) to check for artifacts.

cleaning_steps.title: Calibration check
cleaning_steps.description: Run an indium standard to verify onset temperature (156.6°C) and enthalpy (28.71 J/g).

after_cleaning: Baseline should be flat with no exothermic or endothermic artifacts.
Indium onset should be within ±0.5°C of 156.6°C.
Record cleaning and calibration results.
what_not_to_do: Never use metal tools to scrape the DSC sensor surface.
Do not use water to clean inside the cell — moisture causes baseline artifacts.
Never run reactive or explosive samples without proper safety pans.
Do not exceed the cell's maximum temperature rating during burnout.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Remove pans after each run. Clean cell weekly.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Immediate cleaning if sample has leaked from pan.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Calibrate with indium monthly. Replace thermocouples per manufacturer schedule.

safety_warnings: DSC cells reach very high temperatures — allow complete cooling.
Some samples can decompose violently — use pressure-rated pans for unknowns.
Ensure proper ventilation for evolved gases.
notes: Hermetically sealed pans prevent cell contamination — always crimp properly.
Track baseline quality over time to detect gradual sensor degradation.

cleaning_steps.title: Verify vacuum and imaging
cleaning_steps.description: Re-insert a clean holder, verify vacuum returns to operating level. Take an image of a standard sample (e.g., gold nanoparticles on carbon) to verify resolution.

after_cleaning: Column vacuum should reach operating pressure (typically <1 × 10⁻⁵ Pa).
Lattice fringes on standard sample should be resolved at the instrument's specification.
Record holder cleaning and vacuum levels.
what_not_to_do: NEVER attempt to service the electron gun, column, or vacuum system — contact a service engineer.
Do not insert wet or outgassing samples — they contaminate the column and degrade vacuum.
Never use magnetic tools near the column.
Do not force the holder into the goniometer — misalignment causes vacuum breaks.
Never open the column without authorization and proper training.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Clean holder and plasma clean grids before each session.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Extensive holder cleaning. Schedule column bake-out if contamination persists.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Annual column bake-out and alignment by manufacturer service engineer.

safety_warnings: TEM uses very high voltage (80–300 kV) — never bypass safety interlocks.
The instrument generates X-rays — built-in shielding is present, do not remove panels.
Some TEM samples may be hazardous — follow institutional protocols.
Liquid nitrogen is used for anti-contamination — handle with cryogenic PPE.
notes: User-serviceable parts are limited to sample holders, grids, and aperture cleaning.
Hydrocarbon contamination is the most common cause of poor TEM image quality.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on Raman maintenance from Renishaw inVia, HORIBA LabRAM, and Bruker Senterra documentation.
before_cleaning: Turn off the laser.
Remove the sample from the stage.
Allow the system to power down the laser fully.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean sample stage
cleaning_steps.description: Remove any sample debris. Wipe the stage with a lint-free wipe dampened with ethanol.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean objective lens
cleaning_steps.description: Use a puff of filtered air to remove dust, then gently wipe with lens tissue and optical cleaning solution.
warnings: Use circular motions from center outward. Never dry-wipe an objective lens.

cleaning_steps.title: Inspect optical path
cleaning_steps.description: Check for dust on mirrors and filters. Use filtered air to remove particles.
warnings: Do not touch internal optical components — contact service if contaminated.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean enclosure windows
cleaning_steps.description: If the microscope has enclosure windows, clean with glass cleaner and lint-free wipes.

cleaning_steps.title: Calibration check
cleaning_steps.description: Measure the silicon 520 cm⁻¹ peak. Position should be within ±1 cm⁻¹.

after_cleaning: Silicon peak should be at 520.7 ± 1 cm⁻¹.
Peak intensity should match historical values.
Record calibration results.
what_not_to_do: NEVER look into the laser beam — Raman lasers can cause permanent eye damage.
Do not use regular glass cleaner on optical components — use optical-grade solutions only.
Never attempt to realign the laser or spectrometer optics — this requires trained service.
Do not use fluorescent materials near the instrument during measurements.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Clean stage after each sample. Calibrate with silicon daily.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Clean objective lens and stage immediately.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Annual laser power check and alignment by service engineer.

safety_warnings: LASER HAZARD — Class 3B or 4 laser. Always wear appropriate laser safety eyewear.
Never remove laser safety interlocks or enclosures.
Some samples may fluoresce intensely — reduce laser power to avoid sample damage.
notes: Fluorescence interference is the most common Raman measurement problem — try a different excitation wavelength if available.
Track laser power over time to predict replacement needs.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on ssNMR probe maintenance from Bruker Avance Neo documentation. Most NMR maintenance requires trained specialists.
before_cleaning: Stop rotor spinning and wait for complete stop.
Eject the rotor from the probe.
Turn off spinning gas.
Note the current shim values.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean MAS rotors
cleaning_steps.description: Remove sample from rotors using the unpacking tool. Rinse rotors with ethanol, then dry completely.
warnings: Rotors are precision-machined — do not drop or scratch.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean rotor caps
cleaning_steps.description: Sonicate caps in ethanol for 5 minutes. Dry with lint-free wipes or compressed air.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean probe stator
cleaning_steps.description: Use a gentle puff of air to remove powder from the stator area. If probe allows, carefully wipe accessible surfaces.
warnings: Never insert tools into the probe bore — this damages the coil and stator.

cleaning_steps.title: Check spinning gas lines
cleaning_steps.description: Verify bearing and drive gas pressures are correct. Check for moisture in gas lines.

cleaning_steps.title: Verify with reference
cleaning_steps.description: Pack a rotor with KBr and run a ¹³C CPMAS or adamantane reference to verify probe performance.

after_cleaning: Reference linewidth and sensitivity should match historical values.
Rotor should spin stably at operating speed.
Record probe condition and reference measurements.
what_not_to_do: NEVER approach the magnet with ferromagnetic objects — the strong magnetic field is always on and can be lethal.
Do not attempt to remove or service the probe without proper training.
Never spin a damaged or unbalanced rotor — it can shatter at high speed.
Do not use metal tools near the probe — they can be pulled into the magnet.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Clean rotors and caps between each sample.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Extensive rotor cleaning. If probe is contaminated, schedule service.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Annual probe tuning and maintenance by manufacturer service.

safety_warnings: STRONG MAGNETIC FIELD — never bring metal objects, credit cards, or pacemakers near the magnet.
Rotors spinning at 10,000–110,000 Hz can shatter — always use the safety shield.
Cryogenic liquids (LN₂, LHe) are used — follow cryogenic safety protocols.
Follow your institution's magnet safety zone markings.
notes: Rotor imbalance is the most common cause of spinning instability — always pack rotors symmetrically.
Track reference linewidths to detect probe degradation over time.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on solution NMR maintenance from Bruker Avance Neo and JEOL ECZ series documentation.
before_cleaning: Eject the current sample from the magnet.
Turn off the spinner air.
Note current lock and shim values.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean NMR tubes
cleaning_steps.description: Rinse tubes with appropriate solvent (acetone, then target deuterated solvent). Dry with filtered N₂ stream.
warnings: Never use compressed air from unfiltered lines — oil contaminates tubes.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean sample spinner
cleaning_steps.description: Wipe the spinner (turbine) with a lint-free wipe. Remove any solvent residue. Use a pipe cleaner for the bore.

cleaning_steps.title: Check probe for drips
cleaning_steps.description: Lower the probe (if possible) and inspect for solvent drips from cracked tubes. Wipe clean if found.
warnings: Solvent in the probe degrades performance and can damage electronics.

cleaning_steps.title: Run lineshape test
cleaning_steps.description: Insert a lineshape standard (CHCl₃ in CDCl₃ or acetone-d₆). Run ¹H spectrum and check linewidth.

cleaning_steps.title: Reshim if needed
cleaning_steps.description: If linewidth exceeds specification, run automated shimming (TopShim or equivalent).

after_cleaning: ¹H linewidth on CHCl₃ should meet probe specifications (typically <0.5 Hz for 400 MHz).
Lock should be stable.
Record shim values and lineshape test results.
what_not_to_do: NEVER bring ferromagnetic objects near the magnet — this is a life-threatening hazard.
Do not drop NMR tubes into the magnet bore — use the sample lift system.
Never use cracked or chipped NMR tubes — they can break inside the probe.
Do not ignore spinning sidebands — they indicate a dirty or damaged spinner/tube.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Clean spinner weekly. Lineshape test weekly.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Clean probe bore if solvent spill occurred. Schedule probe cleaning by service if needed.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Cryogen fill schedule per magnet requirements. Annual probe maintenance by manufacturer.

safety_warnings: STRONG MAGNETIC FIELD — keep all ferromagnetic materials away. Follow 5-gauss line safety zone.
Cryogenic liquids (liquid helium, liquid nitrogen) are used for the magnet — follow cryo safety protocols.
Some deuterated solvents are toxic (CDCl₃, benzene-d₆) — use in a fume hood.
In case of magnet quench, evacuate immediately due to oxygen displacement.
notes: NMR tube quality directly affects spectral quality — invest in good tubes.
Track helium level and fill schedule to prevent magnet quench.

source_label: Manufacturer Documentation - Procedure Extracted or Summarized
confidence_note: Based on prep LC maintenance from Agilent 1260 Prep, Waters Prep 150, and KNAUER AZURA documentation.
before_cleaning: Complete any running method.
Remove the prep column — replace with a union.
Drain the fraction collector.
Note pump volumes and current method parameters.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with water
cleaning_steps.description: Pump DI water at 20–50 mL/min (appropriate for your system bore) for 15 minutes to remove buffers.
warnings: Use higher flow rates appropriate for prep-scale tubing.

cleaning_steps.title: Flush with methanol
cleaning_steps.description: Switch to methanol at the same flow rate for 15 minutes.

cleaning_steps.title: IPA flush
cleaning_steps.description: Flush with IPA at reduced flow for 10 minutes for deep cleaning.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean fraction collector
cleaning_steps.description: Remove all tubes/vials. Wipe the collector tray and diverter valve with methanol-dampened wipes.

cleaning_steps.title: Clean injection system
cleaning_steps.description: Flush the injection loop and valve with methanol. For manual injection, clean the injection port.

cleaning_steps.title: Inspect and replace frits
cleaning_steps.description: Check inlet frits for blockage. Replace if system pressure is elevated.

cleaning_steps.title: Return to mobile phase
cleaning_steps.description: Flush back to starting mobile phase conditions. Reconnect column and equilibrate.

after_cleaning: Run a blank injection to verify clean baseline.
Check fraction collector triggering with a test run.
Verify flow rate accuracy (gravimetric check).
Record cleaning and maintenance.
what_not_to_do: Never run prep columns at analytical-scale flow rates — this wastes time and gives poor results.
Do not leave buffers in the system — salt crystallization blocks prep-scale tubing quickly.
Never ignore fraction collector alignment — misaligned tubes cause fraction loss.
Do not use analytical-grade fittings on prep-scale connections — they cannot handle the flow.

cleaning_frequency.routine: Flush system after each purification campaign. Clean fraction collector daily.
cleaning_frequency.after_contamination: Full water → MeOH → IPA → MeOH flush sequence.
cleaning_frequency.preventive: Replace pump seals per manufacturer schedule. Replace check valves annually.

safety_warnings: Prep LC uses large solvent volumes — ensure adequate ventilation and waste capacity.
Organic solvent vapors are flammable — no ignition sources near the instrument.
Large fraction volumes require proper handling and storage.
Wear appropriate PPE when handling large volumes of organic solvents.
notes: Prep LC tubing and fittings are larger bore than analytical — do not interchange.
Always verify fraction purity by analytical LC before combining fractions.
